recordings.remarks: The calls recorded here have come to light via remote-camera survey work. The black currawongs are often interested in the cameras and respond in quite individual ways. This particular currawong returned several times to the camera over a 4-week period and would sometimes (on 4 separate occasions) stand very close, bobbing his/her head below the lens, tapping at the camera case now and then while crooning this unusual 'song' or investigative / interested conversation. The videos the camera takes are 10 seconds long. The recording is of samples from THREE videos taken on Dec 11, 12 and 13, 2024, all recorded at the same location, all between 11am and noon. The location: light forest of tea tree, banksia and eucalypts over a floor of coral lichen in the saddle region between Mounts Roland and Van Dyke, alt 914m. You can hear, on the audio, the occasional beak tap against the camera as well as the crooning / peeping. I've since heard similar peeping sounds in a few other locations but have also collected extensive footage of black currawongs in the area without any hint of it occurring. Note that behaviour recorded by the camera suggests it is the same currawong coming to the camera on each occasion. Also, when I was at the camera in person, a black currawong called at and around me with mild / interested alarm (its more normal call, not the peeping).
